entry.title: Saint-Cast Beach, Brittany
entry.summary: La Grande Plage of Saint-Cast-le-Guildo is a wide beach of fine sand on the north coast of Brittany, with a long promenade and pastel villas behind. The Pointe de la Garde at one end gives a view of the whole bay, and the tide goes out far. The beach is popular with families and sailing schools.

entry.title: Playa de Salobrena, Granada
entry.summary: Playa de Salobrena is a beach of dark sand and fine pebbles on the Costa Tropical, a short drive from the white hill town of Salobrena and its Moorish castle. Sugar cane and sub-tropical fruit grow on the plain behind the coast. The water is clear and the beach is quieter than the resorts further west.

entry.title: Playa de Sancti Petri, Chiclana
entry.summary: Playa de Sancti Petri is a long beach of fine golden sand on the Costa de la Luz, facing a small islet with the ruins of a castle. The tide goes out far and leaves wide sand, and the water is clear. It is a popular beach for walks, windsurfing and sunsets.

entry.title: Stobrec Beach, Split
entry.summary: Stobrec is a former fishing village on the eastern edge of Split, with a pebble beach and a small harbour. The water is clear and the beach is much calmer than the busy city beaches. It is a short drive from the centre of Split.

entry.title: Znjan Beach, Split
entry.summary: Znjan is a long pebble beach on the south-east side of the city of Split, with clear water and a promenade along the shore. It is a favourite with local people, and has cafes, sports areas and showers. The beach is easy to reach by bus from the city centre.

entry.title: Trstenik Beach, Peljesac
entry.summary: Trstenik is a small village on the south coast of the Peljesac peninsula, with a long pebble beach and a little harbour with fishing boats. The water is clear and the pace is slow, far from the main crowds. Vineyards and olive groves cover the hills behind.

entry.title: Okrug Gornji Beach, Ciovo
entry.summary: Okrug Gornji is a village on the island of Ciovo, joined to Trogir by a short bridge. Its beaches are pebble and fine gravel, with calm, clear water and views toward the islands. The long seafront has cafes and restaurants, and a path leads along the coast to nearby coves.

entry.title: Metaponto Beach, Basilicata
entry.summary: Metaponto is a long sandy beach on the Ionian coast of Basilicata, with pine woods behind the dunes and shallow, warm water. The area was a Greek colony in ancient times, and the temple ruins of the Tavole Palatine stand a few kilometres inland.

entry.title: Is Aruttas Beach, Sardinia
entry.summary: Is Aruttas is a beach near Cabras in western Sardinia, known for its coarse sand made of small pink, white and clear quartz grains. The water is clear and shallow, and the sand looks like grains of rice, which gives the beach its fame. Visitors are asked not to take any sand away.

entry.title: Piana di Mattinata Beach, Puglia
entry.summary: Piana di Mattinata is a long beach of sand and fine pebbles below the town of Mattinata on the Gargano coast of Puglia. White limestone hills and olive groves rise behind the shore, and the water is clear and deep. The beach is a base for boat trips to the Baia delle Zagare and the sea caves further north.

entry.title: Fava Beach, Vourvourou
entry.summary: Fava is a sandy beach at Vourvourou on the Sithonia peninsula of Halkidiki, with calm, shallow water and a view of small wooded islands in the bay. Pine trees reach down to the shore and give some shade. Boat trips leave from Vourvourou to the islands and the quiet coves around them.

entry.title: Dafni Beach, Zakynthos
entry.summary: Dafni is a long sandy beach on the Vasilikos peninsula in the south-east of Zakynthos, close to the Gerakas beach where sea turtles nest. The sand is soft and the water shallow, and the bay is quieter than the busy beaches in the north. Hills covered with pine and scrub rise behind.

entry.title: Kapsali Beach, Kythira
entry.summary: Kapsali is the main seaside village of Kythira, with two sheltered bays below the hill town of Chora and its Venetian castle. The main beach is a stretch of sand and fine pebbles beside cafes and tavernas, and the water is calm and clear. Another beach, Fyri Ammos, lies a short walk away.

entry.title: Xlendi Bay, Gozo
entry.summary: Xlendi is a narrow bay on the south-west coast of Gozo, with steep golden cliffs on both sides and a small beach at the head. A promenade with restaurants runs along the water, and the sea is clear and deep for swimming and diving. Cliff walks lead to a watchtower on the headland.

entry.title: Punta Secca Beach, Sicily
entry.summary: Punta Secca is a small fishing village on the south coast of Sicily, with a sandy beach beside whitewashed houses and a lighthouse. The water is shallow and warm, and the village is quiet outside summer. A few fish restaurants sit along the front.

entry.title: Soverato Beach, Calabria
entry.summary: Soverato is a lively seaside town on the Ionian coast of Calabria, with a long beach of pale sand and shallow water. A wide promenade runs behind the sand with bars, shops and restaurants. The beach is popular with Italian families and young people in July and August.

entry.title: Igrane Beach, Makarska Riviera
entry.summary: Igrane is a small village on the southern Makarska Riviera, with a pebble beach and a little harbour below the Biokovo mountain. The sea is clear and the village is quiet compared with the larger resorts to the north. Pine trees give shade along parts of the shore.

entry.title: Viganj Beach, Peljesac
entry.summary: Viganj is a small village on the Peljesac peninsula, facing the island of Korcula across a narrow channel. A steady afternoon wind makes it one of the best places in Croatia for windsurfing and kitesurfing. The beaches are pebbly and the water is clear.

entry.title: Srebreno Beach, Dubrovnik Riviera
entry.summary: Srebreno is a long pebble beach in a sheltered bay on the Dubrovnik Riviera, a short drive south of the old city. The water is calm and clear, and a promenade runs along the shore with cafes and restaurants. It is quieter than the beaches in Dubrovnik itself.

entry.title: Pomena Beach, Mljet
entry.summary: Pomena is a small village at the north-western end of Mljet island, beside the entrance to Mljet National Park. The beaches are small and rocky or pebbly, and the water is clear and deep blue. Pine forest covers the hills, and a path leads to the saltwater lakes inland.

entry.title: Wissant Beach, Cote d Opale
entry.summary: Wissant is a wide, open bay of pale sand on the Opal Coast in northern France, between the headlands of Cap Blanc-Nez and Cap Gris-Nez. Dunes line the back of the beach and the wind makes it a favourite for kitesurfing and sand yachting. On a clear day you can see the white cliffs of England.

entry.title: Plage de Caroual, Erquy
entry.summary: Caroual is a long sandy beach in the bay of Erquy on the north coast of Brittany, with a wide stretch of sand at low tide and pine woods behind. The pink sandstone headland of Cap d Erquy lies just to the east, with heather and coastal paths. The water is cool, and the tide changes the beach a lot.

entry.title: Plage des Dames, Noirmoutier
entry.summary: Plage des Dames is a long beach of fine sand on the island of Noirmoutier, backed by an oak and pine wood and rows of colourful wooden beach huts. The island is linked to the mainland by a bridge and by a tidal causeway called the Passage du Gois. The sea is shallow and the tide goes out far.

entry.title: Pornic Beach, Loire-Atlantique
entry.summary: Pornic is a small harbour town on the Atlantic coast south of the Loire estuary, with a medieval castle above the port and a small sandy beach beside the harbour. The tide goes out far, and the beach is sheltered. Narrow streets climb from the quay with cafes and fish restaurants.

entry.title: Saint-Cyprien Beach, Pyrenees-Orientales
entry.summary: Saint-Cyprien is a long beach of fine sand on the Roussillon coast, with shallow water that is calm for much of the summer. A marina, a promenade and a town centre sit close behind the sand, and the Pyrenees rise on the horizon. The beach is popular with families.

entry.title: Cerbere Beach, Pyrenees-Orientales
entry.summary: Cerbere is the last French town on the Mediterranean coast before the Spanish border, with a pebble beach in a deep bay between steep hills. The sea is clear and the area is part of a marine nature reserve with good snorkelling. A railway station and an old viaduct sit above the village.

entry.title: Plage de Sana, Banyuls-sur-Mer
entry.summary: Banyuls-sur-Mer is a seaside town on the Vermilion Coast near the Spanish border, where terraced vineyards fall steeply to the sea. The town beaches are small and sheltered, with pebbles and some sand, and the water is clear. A marine reserve lies just along the coast, and the town is known for its sweet wine.

entry.title: Sa Tuna Beach, Begur
entry.summary: Sa Tuna is a tiny cove near Begur on the Costa Brava, with a small beach of coarse sand and a row of whitewashed fishermen houses along the shore. Pine-covered cliffs surround the bay and the water is clear. A coast path links Sa Tuna to the neighbouring coves.

entry.title: Cala Gracio, Ibiza
entry.summary: Cala Gracio is a sheltered cove on the west coast of Ibiza, a short drive north of Sant Antoni de Portmany. The sand is coarse and the water is shallow and clear, with pine-covered hills around the bay. It is quieter than the beaches in town, and sunset views are good.

entry.title: Trpanj Beach, Peljesac
entry.summary: Trpanj is a small fishing village at the northern end of the Peljesac peninsula, with a quiet pebble beach beside the harbour. The water is clear and calm, and ferries cross from here to Ploce on the mainland. The village is far from the main tourist routes.
